subject: LLM custody boundary / derivative licensing — decision and next steps
messages:
From: Emma Clark <emma.clark@clearcure.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: ronald.wei@clearcure.com
Date: 2026-05-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood DPA + no-training commitment — clarifying asks

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for the demo last week. Legal flagged a couple of items in the DPA and the term sheet we need to confirm before approval:

- A clear, contractually binding "no-training / no-model-improvement" commitment for all tenant data used via the hosted API (we understand scoped exceptions may exist for aggregated telemetry; want to exclude conversational content and prompts).
- Ownership/derivative rights language: we need to ensure generated outputs are not claimed by Redwood for reuse beyond the customer's use (we're asking for a license to use outputs internally but not for model training or transfer).
- Subprocessor transfers: any new subprocessor that could access processed conversational content must require advance notice and the ability for us to object for 30 days.
- Data egress and escrow: in a worst-case acquisition, we want a technical path to export our tenant data/prompt history and an escrow option for derivative artifacts.

Attached is a short redline from our counsel (ClearCure-DPA-proposed-llm-clauses.docx). Can you confirm operational feasibility and provide any mitigations (e.g., per-tenant ephemeral keys, onshore processing lanes, explicit KMS residency)?

Best,
Emma
Emma Clark
Senior Counsel, ClearCure Health

ClearCure Health | emma.clark@clearcure.com
From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Redwood DPA + no-training commitment — clarifying asks

Emma — thanks for the redline. Short answers up front: yes, we can commit to a contractual no-training/no-model-improvement obligation for conversational data scoped to your tenant, and we can operationalize onshore processing lanes and KMS residency for the workloads you route to those lanes.

A few implementation notes and questions:
- No-training commitment: we would accept a clause that restricts any use of ClearCure tenant conversational content (including prompts and responses) from being used to update or fine-tune models. We will provide the language that maps to our internal feature flag ("learning_disabled_for_tenant").
- Outputs: we propose a customer license granting ClearCure perpetual rights to outputs produced for your use, and an explicit prohibition on Redwood using those outputs for model training or derivative model creation. That mirrors what your redline asks for but we need to confirm the exact license terms you expect.
- Subprocessors: operationally we maintain a subprocessor list and provide 30 days notice prior to onboarding new subprocessors. We can carve out a process that triggers additional review for any subprocessor with access to content (not just telemetry).
- Escrow/export: we can provide a tenant export (SFTP or API) and we offer an optional encrypted escrow of processed interactions on request (we'd need to scope frequency/retention and who pays for escrow storage).

I'm looping in David (ops) and Kimberly (legal) to detail the KMS/residency and finalize the DPA language. Would you be comfortable with a short call tomorrow to close the remaining items?

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Redwood DPA + no-training commitment — clarifying asks

Emma / Lauren — quick legal note to align on contract language that is implementable:

1) No-training clause (suggested):
"Redwood shall not use Customer Content (including prompts and generated outputs) to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any machine learning model used in Redwood's services, except where Customer provides explicit, documented consent in writing."

2) Definitions: we must define Customer Content vs. Telemetry (telemetry = metrics, logs that do not contain prompt/response text) and exclude telemetry from the no-train ban, but telemetry will be handled under the usual pseudonymization safeguards.

3) Subprocessor objection window: we will provide notice of new subprocessors and allow a 30-day objection window. In the event of objection, Redwood will either (a) remove the subprocessor for the customer's processing or (b) provide a mitigation (onshore lane or additional contractual commitments) where feasible.

4) Escrow/export: contractually we can commit to a periodic export and deliver a one-time escrow of tenant artifacts on a paid schedule (we typically do this as a professional-services line item). We'll include clear SLAs for export transfer speeds.

I'll prepare a DPA addendum with the suggested wording and circulate today; David, can you confirm residence/KMS feasibility and any service limits for dedicated onshore lanes?

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Emma Clark <emma.clark@clearcure.com>
Date: 2026-05-26T09:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA + no-training commitment — clarifying asks

Emma — technical ops notes:

- KMS residency: we can provision a tenant-specific KMS key that is restricted to the onshore dedicated lane. Key escrow / HSM options are available for enterprise customers.
- Onshore processing lanes: we can route ClearCure traffic to US-only capacity zones. Those lanes have slightly higher latency variability during peak but will be configured for dedicated throughput.
- Feature flag: toggling learning_disabled_for_tenant is immediate and retroactive for new processing after the flag is set. We cannot retroactively purge derived weights if data has already been used to train prior to the flag — we will ensure the flag is set before go-live.
- Export mechanics: we provide an incremental export API and a one-time full export (JSONL with timestamps, hashed identifiers). For escrow we can provide an encrypted bundle on SFTP or push to a customer-controlled cloud bucket. Delivery SLA depends on export size; typical 100GB export ~48 hours.

Attached is an ops diagram (architecture-kms-residency.pdf) that shows the routing. Happy to walk through on the call.

-David
David Kim
Head of Operations, Redwood Inference
